subject: Crop y-axis in boxplot without changing quantiles

messages.author: d8bf476d5a1db8e7
messages.subject: Crop y-axis in boxplot without changing quantiles
parts:
Hi there,

I am currently conducting a clinical study where I want to visualize
the effect of a medical treatment with different boxplots. I am using
ggplot + geom_boxplot for this task.

Unfortunately, there are some "bad" mavericks in my dataset that are
srewing up the drawing: the boxplot themselves are getting very very
tiny, because ggplot2 also wants to draw the far-outlying mavericks
onto the canvas. I tried to solve the problem by applying the xlim
operator, but the effect is that the mavericks are totally excluded
from the dataset, not only the drawing. This results in a totally
boxplot representation, as the median an the quartiles are affected by
this "cropping".

I wonder if there is a way to simply crop the drawing area, not the
values itself?

Any help is highly appreciated!!!

Thanks & all the best
Philipp

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Crop y-axis in boxplot without changing quantiles
parts:
Hi Philipp,

You can use coord_cartesian(xlim = c(a, b), ylim = c(d, e))

to visually zoom in on a given region.

Regards,

Hadley
